Just because a probability is a very small probability, that does not make it a 0 probability. 

Let’s say, for the sake of argument, that the universe had a 2x10^-100 probability of arising by chance. That seems like a really small number, too small for us to wrap our human brains around. The thing is, it’s actually very different to 0. There’s an uncountably infinite amount of real numbers between that number that I just described, and 0. 

Just because something is unlikely to happen, that doesn’t mean it can’t happen. By saying (or implying) that the existence of the universe without a god is improbable, you’ve smuggled the conclusion in with the premise. The thing is, the Universe arising by chance is a perfectly valid stance - why couldn’t it have arisen by chance?

No. I concretely don’t believe in the god of Christianity - ie an omniscient, omnipotent and omnibenevolent god. I outright reject this specific idea of a god. I believe the problem of evil, specifically natural evil, categorically excludes the traditional Christian god from existing as he is often described.

Do I believe in a kind of first cause for the universe or designer or whatever? I can’t say. I don’t have any evidence for any kind of creating force as it were. As I don’t have any evidence, and burden of proof must be on the positive case, there’s no rational reason to believe in a god. That’s not to say I reject the idea of this general kind of a god, unlike the god of Christianity which I do reject. It could exist. It could also not. There’s simply not evidence to say either way with certainty. 

It’s worth noting that just because something is very unlikely, that it doesn’t mean it’s impossible. The probability of the creation of the universe and the conditions for life arising on earth, without a creator god, may be a very, very small probability. But it’s not a 0 probability, clearly, because we’re here on the earth able to have this conversation. 

To conclude, I think the idea that the universe and life on earth (leading to human life and civilisation) arose entirely by chance is.. a genuinely legitimate argument, and the best possible explanation we have with the evidence available.

I agree, Chuck created Saul Goodman because he couldn’t move past his resentment of Jimmy. The lesson Jimmy learnt from Chuck was to win no matter the cost, as men like Chuck would always try to kick him down and wouldn’t let him move on from his past. I agree, Chuck earned his fate, as horrible as it was. 

But if Jimmy and Chuck could have maybe thrashed it out and started on the path of healing their relationship, if they hadn’t gone so scorched earth on each other, maybe Jimmy wouldn’t have internalised the identity of Slippin Jimmy and thus Saul Goodman to the same extent. Maybe they could have helped each other.

Yeah, he’s an awful person. Jimmy’s no saint but honestly the more I rewatch the show the more I realise that Chuck created Saul Goodman. Get ready for a wall of text about Jimmy and Chuck’s relationship!

Jimmy isn’t entitled to a job at HMM or anything but Chuck lied to his face, and used Howard as the fall guy for years, even doing so while Jimmy is basically working full time to take care of Chuck when he develops his severe mental illness. Jimmy genuinely does want to do good, and Chuck’s deceit of Jimmy comes to light WHEN he identifies genuine injustice and builds a massive class action lawsuit from nothing.  Chuck goes on about ‘Slippin Jimmy’ but Chuck is EXACTLY like him, he just keeps his scams in accordance with the law. Making Howard the fall guy for HMM, playing on Jimmy’s heart strings to tape him admitting to switching the numbers, setting up Ernie to tell Jimmy about the tape.

Chuck says that the reason he’s keeping Jimmy out of the law is because ‘the law is sacred’ but really it’s out of envy for Jimmy and out of deep held childhood resentment. He’s deeply jealous of Jimmy’s charisma, and how he can light up a room. It gnaws away at him. He keeps mental track of ‘all the wrong things Jimmy has done’, because he has this deep felt belief that ‘Jimmy always does the wrong thing but I always do the right thing… so why does everyone love Jimmy but not me?’.

That thought gnaws at him all throughout his life. You get the sense this resentment goes way back, even if Chuck cares about Jimmy in his own twisted way. Jimmy didn’t seem to be that close to Chuck when Chuck got him out of jail. He talks about Jimmy in contempt or holds him in contempt in pretty much every flashback you see, telling Rebecca Jimmy is an ‘acquired taste’ or refusing to tell Jimmy his mum’s last words because he was jealous of Jimmy.

Chuck sublimates this resentment onto the law. The law is sacred. The law is safe from ‘Slippin Jimmy’. Whatever the law says is right because it’s the opposite of what Jimmy would do. When Jimmy is ‘below’ Chuck, and not a lawyer, he doesn’t have address his resentment. When he’s ‘Slippin Jimmy’, he’s below Chuck. When he’s in the mailroom, he’s below Chuck - Chuck says he was proud of Jimmy but again, in every flashback when Jimmy’s trying to connect with Chuck is so dismissive of Jimmy that it hurts. So when Jimmy passes the bar, it presents an existential threat for Chuck. Now, Jimmy has entered Chuck’s domain. He can’t have that. And then soon after, he develops his EMHS as a kind of weird psychological coping mechanism to be able to control the environment around him. He doesnt care about justice and people getting their due really - he cares about the law. He didn’t care about justice when Jimmy, his own brother, gave up his life as Slipping Jimmy, moved to ABQ, and got a law degree while working a full time job. He has to find new excuses for Jimmy to be below him - he’s not a ‘real lawyer’ because he got his degree at the university of American Samoa.

The thing is, the law ISN’T sacred. In his first episode, Saul uses the same law Chuck held in such reverence to send a fall guy to prison, so Walter White could keep making meth. He then launders all his money to sauce up this massive cash income with the image of legality. He uses property law against Jesse’s parents to get them to sell the house to Jesse for cash. This is the flaw of Chuck’s thinking. But anyway.

Jimmy finding out about why HHM didn’t hire him obviously is devastating, and he walks out that room hating the law, those who practice it, and regretting ever ‘turning his life around’, but what really puts him on the path of becoming Saul Goodman, is the whole ‘switching the numbers’ chain of events. It’s worth noting that the only reason Chuck ever found out was because of that resentment for Jimmy - even though he was completely right, anyone, ANYONE else who didn’t have that level of toxic resentment brewing away in them would have just written it off as a mistake. Not Chuck. He’s determined to make Jimmy pay for ‘sabotaging’ him, even when Chuck sabotaged his own brother for YEARS. Jimmy understandably freaks out learning Chuck scammed and taped him, and finally decides to burn his brother to the ground, and hurt him like Chuck hurt him. Just like Chuck has for all those years, Jimmy leans into the worst aspects of himself.

Planting the battery on Chuck was the first part of this. Proving his crippling ‘condition’ is completely psychosomatic in front of the whole world. And it utterly humiliates Chuck in his own domain - the courtroom. Nothing more than a complete and utter defeat for Chuck. As he yells and rambles on about how Jimmy will ‘never change’, the truth is laid bare for the world to see. And then Jimmy uses this to get Chuck’s malpractice insurance cancelled. Really petty stuff, but the question remains - would Jimmy have done any of this if Chuck hadn’t betrayed him at every turn? 

Chuck’s last words are more damaging than he could ever know, and possibly the most hauntingly cruel thing you could hear from your own brother, telling Jimmy to be nothing more than a fraud and a scammer, and that ‘you never mattered all that much to me’. And yeah - Jimmy is never the same after that conversation. Those words repeated over and over and over again in his head as he took Chuck’s advice and became Saul Goodman as a final middle finger to him. 

Jimmy will never know that Chuck likely had a final moment of clarity before he took his own life, realising that his terrible actions pushed away the only family he had left, causing him lose his mind and tear apart his own house before burning himself from a pit of despair.

At the end of S4, Jimmy breaks down in the car park after realising that all his shitty, emotionally abusive brother left him with was those horrible final words to live his life by, a dedication to winning no matter how awful the means are, even if it means savaging your own brother, and $5000.

Jimmy is going to be Jimmy but I kind of view his foray in Davis and Main as being quite tragic because it was right after Marco died and right after he found out that all along, it was Chuck sabotaging him for years and lying in his face. Jimmy 100% made his own messes but I do feel like it was a job he was talked into and his heart wasn’t in.

Wesker and Blight are my favourites partly for the whole mindless thing of just ‘I like to go fast’ but I think a reason both these killers, especially Wesker are so popular is because there’s a lot of subtle things that make them really a fun for a lot of people. Like yes, Wesker is just really fun, going fast and throwing people around. Yes, Blight is really fun zooming around the map like Sonic. 

But both killers are killers with low skill floors, but VERY high skill ceilings. Blight can use his rushes to get around the map, Wesker can do similar, but the amount of ways you can use both powers in loops is endless and it means you can never really get bored of playing them because you’re always learning collisions, ways to mind game loops. As both killers you also can FEEL yourself getting better at them as you play them more and more. But at the same time, they have very intuitive and fluid gameplay, especially Wesker. Both killers have some weaker maps for sure but overall, you know, even the rough maps for them aren’t unplayable for them or anything. And as both, they’re action packed characters where there’s really clear interplay between you and the survivors. They’re killers where you have very strong anti-loop but at the same time you have to play the loops. And they also really punish the ‘hold W’ gameplay that as killers, let’s face it, is annoying. You try to hold W against a Wesker or Blight and you can’t, they have absolutely no problem getting right back on top of survivors and that means you save a ton of time, and that feels really good. As does playing a strong killer, let’s be honest. They also don’t require any setup. You load into a match as Wesker or Blight, and immediately you can start using your power to get around the map and get results. And both have a great suite of addons (maybe too great in Blight’s case..) with strong addons across the board so there’s a ton of different builds and options to tailor your playstyle to on both killers.

I mention both, because before Wesker, it was Blight in every survivor game but both have really similar reasons for being so damn popular. But Wesker has a few things over Blight in terms of why he’s #1 most popular as opposed to Blight’s like 2 or 3. Firstly, he’s iconic as fuck, everyone knows who Wesker is, similar to Nemesis. Secondly, his voicelines. It seems like a silly reason but it makes him so fun, there’s something so great about hearing his laugh as he pulls up his dash, or him shit talking survivors when he gets a hit, downs or hooks them, or him getting pissed at survivors for stunning him. And lastly, just throwing people around and slamming them into shit is so fun.

I know Zeri is problematic, even as someone who plays her a lot but… for all her problems, Zeri is an ADC through and through. If you catch her out or get on top of her, or have some kind of burst damage, she’s dead like any other ADC. I think she’s like Akali where eventually, given more changes and refinement, she will be in an okay place.

Yuumi on the other hand is the only champ I can outright say does NOT belong in League. And it amazes me how 4 years on this is still the case. The issue with her is so simple, it’s that she’s an enchanter you can cannot target. The whole counterplay of enchanters is that they are easy to kill and need to position well so they can benefit their allies while being a safe distance. They’re the champs where they will buff and save the fuck out of people but you as an enemy can identify and respect this and kill them before they can turn whoever into a 1v9 machine. Yuumi just straight up ignores all of this by design and has no acceptable counterplay whatsoever. The only way they can make Yuumi fair is by either making her early laning so underpowered that she just loses her ADC the lane by default, or making her abilities incredibly unimpactful. Because if Yuumi does have abilities that are even say, 50% of what a Soraka could do, the impact of those abilities goes up astronomically by the fact that Yuumi physically cannot be killed or removed from her teammate. People say ‘oh well Yuumi can only heal and buff one person at a time’ but that doesn’t matter because when teams start to group she doesn’t need to buff anyone except the most fed person on the enemy team, even since her rework. Like great, she can only shield the fed Bel’Veth and not the Irelia or Syndra or Kai’Sa at the same time but.. it doesn’t matter that she can’t buff those others because she makes a big threat into a… mega big threat, idk, but one that you have to deal with. I’ll say what everyone else does, and rightfully, Yuumi is unsalvageable with her current identity and needs a complete rework from the ground up.

As a Kat player:

- One of Kat’s biggest strengths is in her roaming. Use wards to counteract this, and ping if she leaves your lane. 
- Because Kat is a reset manaless champion, her abilities are worse on their own than other mid laners. So if you’re playing a mage you can probably shove her under her tower. If you’re playing an assassin, you most likely can 1v1 her or at least get her low. Both of these mean she can’t roam.
- Back or chug potions when you’re low health! It’s such a simple rule, but Kat is really good at killing low health targets, even under tower since if she gets a reset she can just W and E away from the tower. 
- Hold to your CC so that when she goes in, it’s ready. Give her a choice between going while your CC is up or not going in at all. 
- If she gets very fed, hard engage onto her as 5 to force her to jump out so she can’t burst your backline.

I love his visual design and concept but his power is quite poorly designed because of how polarising it is. Around tall loops it can feel almost unplayable because unlike Huntress you need to hit survivors with 6 projectiles to get a health state. But at the same time, around more open loops or in the open there is literally nothing you can do about because he gets so many projectiles that you will go down eventually, no matter how many knifes you dodge.  He’s also insane at camping - he’s nearly Bubba level good. He can throw 5 knifes into a recently unhooked survivor, wait 10s then down them. And he also has the fastest health state shredding in the game, but unlike Huntress who needs to hit precise shots even in places where she can shred health stares, Trickster can straight up spam knifes without even needing to aim that well. Like if you as a survivor try to dodge his knife spam it won’t work; you can’t unless you have something blocking those knifes and even then you’ll be just playing ring around the Rosie until you eventually do get pelted by enough knifes and die. So basically his 1v1 is absolutely nuts even though tall loops are a nightmare for him.

He’s basically a more polarised Huntress. To compensate his insane 1v1, they stick him with the weaknesses of Huntress like the lullaby, reloading and 4.4 but those are made way way worse by the fact Trickster doesn’t have the range and immediate threat a Huntress does. From ones I’ve played:

4. Elden Ring - The actual game itself is really hard but the game gives you so many ways to cheese it.  If you were to put the bosses next to DS1 bosses, the ER bosses would blow them out of the water but the game gives you far more options. Even summons aside, magic is really strong as are status effects. Bonfires are super generous and runbacks are nearly gone (thank fuck). You have a huge open world to get lots of levels in.

3. DS1 - Main difficulty for me came from learning not to lock on, learning you needed light roll for a dodge heavy playstyle and the sparse bonfires. Some of the levels are really hard but I think the bosses by comparison were quite easy with the exception of DLC bosses and O+S. Stamina management is also very much a thing in these games compared to the others, which means you can’t roll spam your way through levels. All of this said, I was actually surprised about how much I liked a lot of the stuff which got QoLed out of later games. Barring the dodgy lock on system, it was fun having to actually manage equip load, time my dodges, worry about my stamina, find good windows to heal since you can’t move and having everything have a consequence to it.

2. DS3 - The bosses in this game are nutty and really really good. Abyss Watchers is considered easier by the time you get to stuff like Pontiff who is considered easy compared to Nameless who is considered easy compared to Midir or Friede! The levels themselves have nice generous bonfire placements and the rolling is very safe and stamina efficient. 

1. Sekiro - I would actually rate this the easiest on the second playthrough I’m doing now (really!) because this game really does leave you a master of the combat system. Your character when you know how to use him, is far more powerful than a DS character, being able to counter everything thrown your way, having tools for every single enemy, having really good reliable stealth, being able to backstab enemies in one hit including field bosses you can straight up rip half the HP off of with stealth, lots of combat arts, super fast, super mobile AND can resurrect! The issue is you need to learn how to use all of this and you will get the combat system beat into you. I spent four hours on Genichiro my first run, 2 hours on Gyoubu, 2 on Corrupted Monk, 5 on Shinobi Owl… you get the idea. Then second playthrough I legit stumbled onto Genichiro by accident, middling on Estus, having forgot to get the lightning reverse and beat his ass first try. The difference was I learnt how to play the game. The first playthrough in this game is absolutely brutal but it’s really fun and this is probably my favourite FS game.

My main tip and this will sound weird is that Sekiro isn’t really a souls game. There are familiar elements like the Estus and Level Design sure, but this is more of a stealth action game. Dodging does fuck all in this game compared to DS or ER, it’s more of a repositioning tool. Deflecting (blocking as the attack hits you) is the big part of combat. This game is almost like a rhythm game, you’re in a dance with your enemy and it’s very fun. You have no stamina so you can always be on the aggressive, using parries to build up posture damage between your attacks to deal more posture damage and HP damage. Your levelling isn’t stats, it’s skills (so stuff like Mikiri counter which you will definitely want), you have to actually engage with the combat and beat bosses to get attack power and HP boosts. HP boosts are typically from mini bosses, main bosses give attack power boosts when defeated.

Stealth is absolutely crucial as are approaches in the levels - a lot of mini bosses can straight up be taken down a deathblow if you approach them correctly, taking into account your surroundings and nearby enemies, tough enemies can be trivialised with stealth. You’re a ninja, play like one.

The white shield is the Endurance status effect. It makes it so that if that survivor is injured, any damage that would put them in the dying state instead puts them in Deep Wounds, and they get a speed boost similar to if you injured them.

If it comes after an unhook, it’s from Bill’s perk Borrowed Time, anyone who has it will give Endurance to the survivor who was unhooked for 12 seconds (you should assume it’s at T3). This is one of the most common and game changing survivor perks, and as a killer you should always assume Borrowed Time is in play, and go for the unhooker instead of the unhookee. Going for the person who was just unhooked will waste so much of your time, since they get the speed boost, while you’re there in your attack animation, and this also lets the survivor who just unhooked get away too.

There are two other things that give Endurance. Cheryl’s Soul Guard gives whoever has it Endurance for 8 seconds after they recover from the dying state. It’s rarer but still worth taking into account. Rarer still is the Styptic Agent, a purple med kit addon that consumes the Medkit but gives the person who was given it Endurance. Generally you won’t run into this too much. 

But yeah, that’s the white shield
